title: Gaussian gradient bound from mean rotational variation
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be Fréchet differentiable everywhere with derivative $L(x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ at $x$, and suppose that $x\mapsto L(x)$ is continuous and $0\le f(x)\le 1$ for every $x$. Let $C\in[0,\infty]$. If for every real $\theta>0$, $\sqrt{\pi/2}$ times the Gaussian mean of $|f(\cos\theta\,z_1+\sin\theta\,z_2)-f(z_1)|$, divided by $\theta$, is at most $C$ (with that real quantity embedded in $[0,\infty]$), then $\int \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n (L(x)e_i)^2}\,d\gamma_n(x)\le C$, as a nonnegative extended integral.
hypotheses_covered: $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ has derivative $L(x)$ at every $x$
The derivative map $x\mapsto L(x)$ is continuous
For every $\theta>0$, the real Gaussian mean variation bound, embedded in $[0,\infty]$, is at most $C$
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$ and $X,Y$ independent with that law. Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable everywhere with derivative $L(x)$, and put $|L(x)|_2=\sqrt{\sum_i(L(x)e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ is the canonical basis. Assume $L$ is continuous, $0\le f\le1$, and $C\in[0,\infty]$. If $\sqrt{\pi/2}\,\mathbb E|f(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y)-f(X)|/\theta\le C$ for every $\theta>0$, where the real expectation is embedded into $[0,\infty]$, then the nonnegative extended expectation satisfies $\mathbb E|L(X)|_2\le C$.
